categories.main_business_segments: MGM Resorts International operates three primary business segments: Las Vegas Strip Resorts (nine casino properties including Aria, Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan, MGM Grand Las Vegas, Mandalay Bay, Luxor, Excalibur, New York-New York, and Park MGM), Regional Operations (eight casino properties across the United States including properties in Detroit, Mississippi, New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts, New York, and Ohio), and MGM China (56% ownership stake in two Macau casino properties: MGM Macau and MGM Cotai). The company also operates global online gaming through LeoVegas and a 50% stake in BetMGM, plus a 50% interest in Osaka IR KK for a planned integrated resort in Japan.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: MGM Resorts operates casino gaming facilities featuring slot machines, table games, and electronic gaming devices, complemented by state-of-the-art hotel operations, convention facilities, and entertainment venues. The company leverages advanced data science and analytics capabilities for customer experience optimization, employs a loyalty technology platform enabling points earning through gaming and non-gaming activities, and utilizes digital commerce technology for customized package sales. Technology infrastructure includes digital check-in processes, mobile adoption platforms, and omni-channel customer engagement systems integrated across physical properties and digital platforms.
categories.primary_customers_markets: MGM Resorts serves diverse customer segments including premium gaming customers, leisure and wholesale travel customers, business travelers, and group customers (conventions, trade associations, small meetings). Primary markets include Las Vegas (domestic leisure and convention travelers, Far East high-end gaming customers), regional U.S. markets (local and regional gaming customers), and Macau (primarily main floor gaming customers from mainland China and Asia-Pacific region). The company targets upper-end market segments while also catering to leisure and value-oriented customers through its diverse property portfolio.
categories.geographic_coverage: MGM Resorts operates primarily in the United States with major concentration on the Las Vegas Strip (nine properties) and regional U.S. locations (eight properties across Michigan, Mississippi, New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts, New York, and Ohio). Internationally, the company has significant operations in Macau through a 56% stake in MGM China (two properties), a growing presence in the United Kingdom through BetMGM's 2023 launch, and a planned integrated resort development in Osaka, Japan through a 50% ownership in Osaka IR KK. The company also has non-gaming management agreements for branded properties in the United Arab Emirates.
categories.supply_chain_position: MGM Resorts operates primarily in the downstream/end-consumer segment of the hospitality and gaming industry, directly operating casino resorts and providing gaming, hotel, dining, and entertainment services to end customers. The company leases real estate assets for domestic properties under triple-net lease agreements with VICI Properties and other landlords, positioning it as an operator rather than owner of most domestic properties. For online gaming, the company operates through consolidated subsidiary LeoVegas and joint venture BetMGM, distributing gaming products through digital channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: MGM Resorts' strategic priorities center on five pillars: (1) Strong People and Culture through talent recruitment and diversity/inclusion initiatives, (2) Customer-Centric Model leveraging brand strength and customer insights, (3) Gaming Entertainment innovation and product distribution across the broadest addressable market, (4) Operational Excellence through digital capability enhancement and margin expansion, and (5) Disciplined Capital Allocation maximizing shareholder value. Key R&D and growth initiatives include developing an integrated resort in Japan, expanding BetMGM as a leader in online sports betting and iGaming, growing international digital presence through LeoVegas and BetMGM brands, exploring full-scale commercial gaming in New York, and pursuing gaming expansion opportunities in the UAE.
categories.revenue_model: MGM Resorts generates revenue primarily through casino gaming operations (table games and slot machines), hotel room rentals, food and beverage services, entertainment and retail offerings, and convention/meeting space utilization. For Las Vegas Strip Resorts, over half of net revenue derives from non-gaming operations (hotel, food and beverage, entertainment, retail). Regional Operations derive the majority of revenue from gaming operations. The company also generates revenue through online gaming and sports betting via BetMGM and LeoVegas, and management fees from international properties. Most revenue is cash-based through customer wagering or payment for services via cash or credit cards.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: MGM Resorts competes with major gaming and hospitality companies including other large casino operators on the Las Vegas Strip and in regional markets, as well as smaller hotel offerings and peer-to-peer rental platforms. In Macau, the company competes with five other gaming concessionaires and casinos in other Asian gaming centers (Singapore, South Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, Philippines, Australia). In online gaming, BetMGM faces competition from other iGaming and sports betting operators and the broader gaming/entertainment industries. The company positions itself as a premium operator of high-quality resorts with recognized brands, superior amenities, and distinctive entertainment offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: MGM Resorts is a large-cap gaming company with 2023 net revenues of $16.2 billion (23% increase from 2022's $13.1 billion) and operating income of $1.9 billion (31% increase from 2022). The company operates 44,654 guestrooms across 16 domestic properties and two Macau properties (56% owned). As of December 31, 2023, MGM Resorts had approximately 45,000 full-time and 18,000 part-time domestic employees, plus 12,000 at MGM China and 1,000 at LeoVegas. The company carries approximately $6.4 billion in consolidated debt and has been executing an asset-light business model involving property divestitures and strategic acquisitions to unlock capital and improve financial flexibility.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: MGM Resorts emphasizes premium quality and distinctive brand positioning through several key differentiators: (1) High-quality resort properties with luxurious guestrooms, state-of-the-art convention facilities, and premier dining/entertainment/retail amenities, (2) Unique 'must-see' entertainment attractions and experiences, (3) Superior customer service through well-trained, motivated employees, (4) Distinctive marketing and customer loyalty programs (MGM Rewards tiered program), (5) Digital innovation and omni-channel integration connecting physical properties with online gaming/sports betting, (6) Strategic property locations in desirable leisure and business travel markets, and (7) Commitment to corporate social responsibility, environmental sustainability, and responsible gaming practices that enhance brand reputation and customer trust.
